identity.name: Bai-Kakaji Polymers Limited
identity.industry: Plastic & Polymer Packaging (rigid PET preforms/closures + flexible films)

summary.oneLiner: Bai-Kakaji is a Latur-based integrated plastic-packaging maker (rigid PET preforms/closures + flexible films) that did a Dec-2025 IPO (₹105 cr) to slash leverage (D/E 2.04→0.37) and fund a strategic pivot into higher-value flexible films; FY26 revenue ₹365 cr with 13.4% EBITDA margin and a deleveraged, cash-generating balance sheet, targeting ₹1,000 cr turnover by FY29 via a ₹100 cr capex (65% to flexible).

one-line thesis: Bai-Kakaji is a Latur-based integrated plastic-packaging maker (rigid PET preforms/closures + flexible films) that did a Dec-2025 IPO (₹105 cr) to slash leverage (D/E 2.04→0.37) and fund a strategic pivot into higher-value flexible films; FY26 revenue ₹365 cr with 13.4% EBITDA margin and a deleveraged, cash-generating balance sheet, targeting ₹1,000 cr turnover by FY29 via a ₹100 cr capex (65% to flexible).
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹365 cr | 16.4% 3-yr CAGR | No QoQ/Q4-specific split disclosed in report |
| EBITDA / margin | ₹48.78 cr (13.36%) | — | |

| Gross margin | n/d | — | Not disclosed |
| Order book | n/d | — | Not an order-driven model; FMCG/beverage demand-led |
| Cash / net debt | D/E 0.37 (FY26) vs 2.04 (FY25); OCF +₹28.04 cr | sharply deleveraged | Post-IPO balance-sheet transformation |
> Figures are FY26 annual (not isolated Q4); document gives no quarterly bridge. One-off: Dec-2025 IPO ₹105 cr drove the deleveraging.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- Revenue: target **₹1,000 cr turnover by FY29** (vs ₹365 cr FY26).
- Capex: **₹100 cr plan underway** — 65% flexible packaging, 35% rigid.
- Margin: no explicit target (FY26 EBITDA 13.36%); pivot to flexible films positioned as higher-value.
- Capacity / commissioning: 7.2 MW solar expansion to cut power costs; flexible-film capacity build-out.
- Utilization: 90%+ PET preforms, 84% closures.
order book & pipeline: Demand-led (no formal order book). Diversified across National, Regional and Local brand segments. Marquee clients: Parle Agro (Bailley), Campa (Reliance), Patanjali, JSW, Tata, Daawat, Clear, Sunrich. Approved/officially listed supplier to IRCTC.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Rigid:** PET preforms 22,600 MTPA; caps/closures >500 cr pieces/yr (output). End-markets: beverages, FMCG, edible oil, dairy, pharma.
- **Flexible (incl. Mundada Polymer subsidiary):** Shrink film 4,500 MTPA, Coating film 2,340 MTPA, Stretch film 1,620 MTPA; plus adhesive films and BOPP labels.
- **Mundada Polymer** (acquired Feb 2026, wholly-owned) — enables "one-stop" rigid + flexible solution.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Strategic pivot to flexible packaging (65% of ₹100 cr capex) — larger TAM (flexible ₹1.70 lakh cr vs rigid ₹1.26 lakh cr in India plastic packaging).
- Regional/local brand expansion thesis — structural shift as regional players scale; post-COVID demand for cost-effective packaging.
- Weight-saving closure innovation (in-house tool room): cap weight cut 1.8g → 1.15g — cost + carbon advantage.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA 13.36%, PAT 7.39%. Power-cost reduction via 7.2 MW solar. High utilization (90%+ preforms). Lightweighting reduces resin/material per unit. Resin (PET/polymer) is the key input — crude/petchem-linked cost exposure not quantified in report.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): ₹100 cr capex (65% flexible / 35% rigid) + 7.2 MW solar. Five European-equipped manufacturing units in Latur (4 rigid, 1 flexible). Machinery from Husky, Sacmi, Windmöller & Hölscher.
capital allocation: Dec-2025 IPO ₹105 cr deployed to deleverage (D/E 2.04→0.37), fund solar + capacity. Feb-2026 acquisition of Mundada Polymer (wholly-owned). OCF turned positive (+₹28.04 cr).
risks & watch-items:
- Single-cluster manufacturing concentration (all units in Latur).
- Resin/polymer (crude-linked) input-cost volatility — not hedged/quantified.
- Customer concentration in beverages/FMCG; pricing pressure from large national brands.
- Plastic-packaging regulatory/ESG (EPR, single-use plastic norms) overhang.
- Execution risk on the ~3x revenue ramp to ₹1,000 cr by FY29 and flexible-segment scale-up.
- This is a self-prepared promotional analysis report, not an audited/Q&A call — verify claims against actual filings.
management quality / tone: Tone is promotional/IR (event marketing report). Credible operational specifics (named European OEMs, MTPA capacities, marquee clients, utilization). No management voices quoted; no analyst scrutiny. Clear capital-discipline narrative (IPO → deleverage).
non-obvious takeaways:
- IRCTC approved-supplier status is a quiet moat/quality signal.
- Lightweighting (1.8g→1.15g) is both a margin and a sustainability lever, and a client-stickiness tool via customized closure development.
- Pivot economics: flexible has larger Indian TAM but is more fragmented/competitive — margin sustainability is the key unknown.
- Picks-and-shovels read: leveraged to beverage/FMCG/edible-oil/dairy volume growth rather than any electrification/grid theme.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
